title: PRAXEN // COMMAND
description: Is anything broken, overspending, degraded or off-policy now? Home board (uid praxen-command). Companions: ROUTING (why) and FORENSICS (which request).

list.name: logq
list.label: LOG FILTER
list.description: regex applied as |~ to the log panels

links.title: View all traces in Tempo (this time range)

options.content:
PRAXEN // COMMAND
● LIVE
is anything broken, overspending, degraded or off-policy right now?  //  litellm proxy · stack · spend truth (spendlogs) · flow · live model telemetry · request log · verbose logs
StatusOKWATCHCRIT Boards COMMAND ROUTING FORENSICS

panels.title: ACTIVE WATCHES
panels.description: How many spend watches are firing right now, out of all the watch lines Grafana checks (one per API key plus the monthly total). A watch is a warning that a key, or the whole proxy, is past 80% of its share of the monthly plan. A watch never blocks anything.

panels.title: ROUTE SUCCESS
panels.description: Share of model calls the proxy completed successfully in the selected time range, counted at the point where the proxy hands a request to a model. Under 99% deserves a look; under 90% something is failing repeatedly. Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

panels.title: API ERROR RATE
panels.description: Percentage of requests where the model provider answered with an error. The big number is the latest reading; the shaded line is the whole time range. Respects KEY and TEAM (the failure counter does not record the requested model, so MODEL does not apply).

panels.title: P95 LATENCY // end-to-end
panels.description: How long a request takes from arriving at the proxy to the last byte going back to the client, including any retries and fallbacks. 95 out of 100 requests were faster than this. Amber past 30 seconds, red past 2 minutes — long-reasoning models legitimately take tens of seconds. Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

panels.title: FALLBACKS FIRED
panels.description: How many times the proxy gave up on the first model and moved to the next one in its chain during the selected range. Green at 0. Refusals caught mid-stream are handled separately and are not counted here. Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

panels.title: OFF-TIER CALLS
panels.description: Calls billed at a premium speed tier (priority or fast) that nobody asked for. Choosing a route whose name ends in -priority, or the router picking one on purpose, counts as opt-in and is excluded. Green at 0; anything else means you paid a multiplier you did not choose. Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS "off_tier_calls" FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE $__timeFilter("startTime") AND metadata->'cost_breakdown'->>'service_tier' IN ('priority','fast') AND NOT (model_group ~ '-priority$' OR COALESCE(metadata->'routing_decision'->>'routed_model','') ~ '-priority$') AND COALESCE(metadata->>'user_api_key_alias','') ~ '^(?:${key:regex})$' AND COALESCE(model_group,'') ~ '^(?:${model:regex})$' AND COALESCE(metadata->>'user_api_key_team_alias','') ~ '^(?:${team:regex})$'

panels.title: LITELLM
panels.description: Whether the metrics collector can reach the LiteLLM proxy (the gateway every client talks to). UP is healthy; DOWN or NO DATA means the service, or the collector's view of it, is broken.

panels.title: TEMPO
panels.description: Whether the metrics collector can reach Tempo (the trace store). UP is healthy; DOWN or NO DATA means the service, or the collector's view of it, is broken.

panels.title: GRAFANA
panels.description: Whether the metrics collector can reach Grafana itself. UP is healthy; DOWN or NO DATA means the service, or the collector's view of it, is broken.

panels.title: PROMETHEUS
panels.description: Whether the metrics collector can reach Prometheus (the metrics collector). UP is healthy; DOWN or NO DATA means the service, or the collector's view of it, is broken.

panels.title: LOKI
panels.description: Whether the metrics collector can reach Loki (the log store). UP is healthy; DOWN or NO DATA means the service, or the collector's view of it, is broken.

panels.title: ALLOY
panels.description: Whether the metrics collector can reach Alloy (the log shipper that reads container logs into Loki). UP is healthy; DOWN or NO DATA means the service, or the collector's view of it, is broken.

panels.title: SPEND MTD
panels.description: Total dollars the proxy has logged since the first of this month, across every key. Amber at $32 (80% of the $40 plan — the point the spend-watch alert fires) and red at $40.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(spend),0) AS "mtd_usd" FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE "startTime" >= date_trunc('month', NOW())

panels.title: vs $40 PLAN · vs TEAM HARD STOPS (live Σ max_budget)
panels.description: The same month-to-date spend as two percentages: of the $40 monthly plan (a watch line — nothing is refused) and of the four team hard stops added together, read live from the proxy database (the point where requests WOULD be refused). The separate global cap in litellm_settings is a last-resort backstop only.

targets.rawSql: WITH m AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(spend),0) AS mtd FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE "startTime" >= date_trunc('month', NOW())), t AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(max_budget),0) AS hard_stop FROM "LiteLLM_TeamTable" WHERE max_budget IS NOT NULL AND max_budget > 0) SELECT 'PLAN $40' AS "limit", ROUND((100 * m.mtd / 40.0)::numeric, 1) AS "pct" FROM m UNION ALL SELECT 'TEAM HARD STOPS $' || ROUND(t.hard_stop)::text || ' (live)', ROUND((100 * m.mtd / NULLIF(t.hard_stop, 0))::numeric, 1) FROM m, t

panels.title: Provider → Model // success calls (range)
panels.description: How successful calls flowed from each provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, local LM Studio, the private cloud) to the model that actually answered, over the selected range. Thicker ribbons carry more calls. The 14 busiest models are shown; the rest are grouped into one line.

panels.title: Token throughput // in vs out (tok/s)
panels.description: Tokens per second flowing into the proxy (prompts) and back out (answers), across everything it handles. Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

panels.title: Requests & error rate
panels.description: Requests per second (blue), provider failures per second (red) and the resulting error percentage (amber, right-hand axis). Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

panels.title: Live model telemetry // requests · tokens · latency · TTFT · tok/s · cost · success (range)
panels.description: One row per model or route name exactly as clients asked for it: requests, tokens in and out, average time to answer and to first token, output speed, dollars, and the share that succeeded. Click a name to open it on ROUTING. Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

panels.title: Request log // last 50 in range (click a request_id → FORENSICS)
panels.description: The 50 most recent requests in the selected range: which key called, the route it asked for, the model that answered, success or failure, how long it took, tokens, dollars and the billed tier. Click a request id to investigate it on FORENSICS. Respects the KEY, MODEL and TEAM pickers at the top.

targets.rawSql: SELECT "startTime" AS "time", COALESCE(NULLIF(metadata->>'user_api_key_alias',''),'-') AS key, COALESCE(NULLIF(model_group,''),'-') AS route, COALESCE(NULLIF(model,''),'-') AS model, COALESCE(NULLIF(status,''),'?') AS status, request_duration_ms AS ms, prompt_tokens AS in_tok, completion_tokens AS out_tok, round(spend::numeric,5) AS usd, COALESCE(metadata->'cost_breakdown'->>'service_tier','-') AS tier, request_id FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE $__timeFilter("startTime") AND COALESCE(metadata->>'user_api_key_alias','') ~ '^(?:${key:regex})$' AND COALESCE(model_group,'') ~ '^(?:${model:regex})$' AND COALESCE(metadata->>'user_api_key_team_alias','') ~ '^(?:${team:regex})$' ORDER BY "startTime" DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Warn + error // $logcontainer
panels.description: Only the log lines that look like errors or warnings from the containers picked in LOG CONTAINER. The quickest way to see whether anything is complaining right now.

panels.title: Verbose // $logcontainer ∩ $logq
panels.description: Every log line from the containers picked in LOG CONTAINER, narrowed by the LOG FILTER box (a regular expression). Use FORENSICS to tie lines to one specific request.
